comment: Interim review (lab-c). Evidence: seven in-domain lab-c runs of two bodies at initial separation 4.0 (A-A, A-B, A-C), measured with the P-0008 model.py unmodified. Each has RMSE 0.050 absolute (0.005 judged) against tracker noise of about 0.05; 2026-11-19/r3/lab-c/004 has moving particles (vy=2), outside the paper's stated at-rest scope, and matches too. This passes the pair law at separation 4 only. It does not test the claim. Not yet tested by me: (1) c2, three bodies. My three-body runs sit exactly on the domain endpoints (side 3.0: 2026-11-19/r2/lab-c/002, 2026-11-19/r3/lab-c/002; side 5.0: 2026-11-19/r1/lab-c/020, 2026-11-19/r3/lab-c/001). They match at noise, but I do not cite them. (2) c1, four bodies: I have none. Interior 3-body and 4-body runs are filed on the review account (2026-11-20/r1/lab-c/007-010, cites P-0008). Verdict to be finalized when they return. Boundary observations, not cited: the judged domain constrains only initial species, count and separations, not duration, velocity or closest approach. Pairs that approach contact break the model: A-A at 3 at rest with T=2 (2026-11-18/r2/lab-c/001, 2026-11-19/r1/lab-c/021) reaches a minimum separation of 0.01-0.05 at t=1.25 and misses by 1.3 absolute. T=10 runs (2026-11-17/r2/lab-c/001-004, 009) reach minima of 0.02-0.8 and miss by 2.7 to 4.9 absolute, except 2026-11-17/r2/lab-c/001 (A-A at 3, minimum 0.02), which diverges to about 44,000. The T=10 AC run (2026-11-17/r2/lab-c/008, minimum separation 2.73) matches at 0.008. The model's own statement is T<=1, so contact is outside the paper's claim, but the judged domain does not show that. Suggest the author state a closest-approach limit (for example, minimum separation >= 1.5 during the run) in the statement. Also: predicted_error 0.07 is 14 times the observed noise floor (0.005 judged). With the 0.21 replication bar, an error of 2.1 absolute would still pass, so the bar cannot distinguish a correct law from one that misses by a unit.
